title: Cocktail 2 Just Got an 'A' Certificate. It's Kriti Sanon's First Adult Film Ever.
excerpt: Advance bookings opened at midnight, Delhi premiere is Thursday, and Shahid Kapoor says he's finally playing someone you'd actually want to grab a drink with.
body:
The censor board has spoken, and it's official: Cocktail 2 is not your wholesome family outing. The film starring Shahid Kapoor, Kriti Sanon, and Rashmika Mandanna has been cleared by the Central Board of Film Certification with an 'A' certificate — adults only — and as of midnight on June 14, advance bookings are live across India.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=XXxUqLHq1xg

This is a first for Kriti Sanon. In twelve years and two dozen-plus films, she has never carried an adult rating. For Rashmika, it's her second after Animal. And for Shahid, it's the fifth time — following Kaminey, Udta Punjab, Kabir Singh, and the recent O'Romeo — which means he now has two consecutive adult-rated releases, a career first. The original Cocktail from 2012, with Saif, Deepika, and Diana Penty, was U/A. The sequel, clearly, has different ambitions.

!Kriti Sanon — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

*"Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter India*, he described his character with something approaching tenderness:
"After very long I'm playing a character that's not alpha, hard, or grey and edgy."**

The runtime clocks in at a generous 150 minutes — four minutes longer than the original — which suggests director Homi Adajania isn't rushing the love triangle between Kunal, Ally, and Diya. And if Shahid's own words are anything to go by, this isn't just more romantic chaos. Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter India, he described his character with something approaching tenderness:

"After very long I'm playing a character that's not alpha, hard, or grey and edgy. I'm playing an extremely likeable, warm and endearing character." — Shahid Kapoor

That's a striking confession from an actor who has built much of his recent identity on intensity. After the moody Kabir Singh. After the feral Romeo in O'Romeo. After Deva, which underperformed. Shahid is softening — and he's doing it publicly, as if recalibrating his career in front of us. He recently admitted that the back-to-back disappointments of Deva and O'Romeo fundamentally changed how he chooses scripts, telling interviewers he now insists on having team members present during narrations because he no longer trusts his own solitary instincts.

!Rashmika Mandanna — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

The music is already doing its job. Pritam's soundtrack, with lyrics by Amitabh Bhattacharya, has been dropping singles steadily. Mashooka, an energetic romantic number shot in Sicily, features Shahid and Kriti in sun-drenched Italian landscapes that look like they cost someone a lot of money. Tujhko, sung by Arijit Singh, is the emotional anchor — a track centred on Shahid and Rashmika's dynamic that reportedly left journalists teary during a private preview. The film reunites Shahid with Kriti after the surprise success of Teri Baaton Mein Aisa Uljha Jiya, and pairs him with Rashmika for the first time — a combination the internet has been loudly anticipating.

The premiere is set for Delhi on June 18 — a Thursday-night event that insiders are calling one of the capital's biggest celebrity gatherings this year. The entire cast, along with Homi, producers Dinesh Vijan and Luv Ranjan, and the music team are expected. Given how central the soundtrack is to this franchise's DNA — the first Cocktail gave us "Tumhi Ho Bandhu," after all — expect the premiere to be as much a musical event as a cinematic one.

Trade projections are cautiously optimistic. Boxoffy pegs the opening day between ₹8–11 crore, with a weekend forecast of ₹28–38 crore. The film currently sits at #1 on IMDb's real-time list of most anticipated Indian titles, with a 21% page-view share. Over 29,500 users have marked it "Interested" on BookMyShow. The Hype Index stands at 66 — strong, if not overwhelming.

For diaspora audiences, the question is simpler: when can you see it? Cocktail 2 releases globally on June 19, and international bookings through Maddock Films' distribution network should open in the coming days. Given the franchise's urban, English-comfortable demographic, expect strong opening-weekend showings in the US, UK, Canada, and the Gulf — the NRI corridors where Shahid, Kriti, and Rashmika all command dedicated fanbases.

The A certificate will keep families with younger children away, but for everyone else, the signal is clear: Cocktail 2 isn't playing safe. Five days to go.
